name: High-Low Split Poker
description: High-Low Split is a fundamental poker pot-splitting mechanic rather than a standalone game. It is commonly applied to variants like Omaha and Seven Card Stud. In these games, the pot is divided into two halves: one for the best 'high' hand and one for the best qualifying 'low' hand (usually 8-or-better).

overview.description: High-Low Split is a fundamental poker pot-splitting mechanic rather than a standalone game. It is commonly applied to variants like Omaha and Seven Card Stud. In these games, the pot is divided into two halves: one for the best 'high' hand and one for the best qualifying 'low' hand (usually 8-or-better).

history.origins: The high-low split format emerged in the mid-20th century as a way to make poker games more dynamic and keep more players in the hand. It added a separate layer of strategy alongside traditional high-hand play.
timeline: 1970s: High-low variants become standard in high-stakes mixed games.
1980s: Omaha Hi-Lo (8-or-better) is popularized in casinos.
Present: A staple of the World Series of Poker and online mixed game rotations.
history.cultural: Known for 'action' games where pots can grow very large because multiple players have a chance to win at least half.
history.evolution: The '8-or-better' qualifier was introduced to prevent players from winning the low half with mediocre low hands, forcing tighter play.

setup.dealing: Deal and betting rounds follow the base game variant (e.g. Omaha or Stud). After the final round, hands are revealed for high and low.

rules.objective: Win either the high half of the pot, the low half, or both ('scoop').
rules.gameplay:
1. Play proceeds according to the specific variant (e.g., Omaha or Stud).
2. After the final betting round, players reveal their hands.
3. Identify the best high hand and the best qualifying low hand.
4. **Scooping**: If one player has both the best high and the best low, they take the entire pot.
5. If multiple players tie for a half, they split that half (quartering).
keyRules: Deal and betting follow the base variant (e.g. Omaha or Stud).
At showdown, best high hand uses standard poker rankings; best low hand qualifies with no card above 8 (eight-or-better), ace low, straights and flushes do not count.
Pot splits equally between best high and best qualifying low; ties split that half; one player can scoop both halves.
The cards speak for themselves; no declaration of high or low required.

strategy.basic: Prioritize hands that have 'scoop potential'. A hand that can only win the low half is much less valuable than one that can win both.
strategy.intermediate: Avoid 'middle' cards (9, 10, J); they don't help with low hands and aren't strong enough for top-tier high hands.
strategy.advanced: Positional play is critical. Being able to see how many people are chasing the low half helps you decide whether to bluff the high side or value-bet your low.
tips: The 'Nut Low' (the best possible low hand given the board) is your best friend.
In Omaha Hi-Lo, never play hands like 4-5-6-7; they are 'too high for low and too low for high'.
